## Natural history notes

A medium-sized tiger moth characterized by pale yellowish to tan wings crossed with faint darker bands, a fuzzy body, and a soft resting posture with the wings held roof-like over the back. In Florida, the Banded Tussock Moth is found in hardwood forests, hammocks, pine-oak woods, forest edges, parks, yards, and wooded neighborhoods where host trees and shrubs occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the hairy caterpillars feed on a variety of woody plants, including oaks, hickories, walnuts, and other hardwoods, and should be handled cautiously because their hairs can irritate skin.
